answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Lifeguard certification with aquatic safety attestation flips the bet — a certification number renewed every two years — and the kernel lands on the attacker instead. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the terrace of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The nebula grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
